Twitter accused of deliberately allowing its platform to be cluttered with Russian propaganda in run up to US Midterms.
According to a legal complaint filed on Sunday by US-based Democracy Integrity Project (DIP) and viewed by The Guardian, Twitter was indifferent to the spread of Russian propaganda on its platform in the run up to the US Midterm elections in 2018.
The group also alleges that Twitter provided its account information to Russian operatives.
The complaint, filed at the US District court for the District of Columbia, asks for an injunction ordering Twitter executives to appear in court to explain how they allowed foreign threats to spread propaganda.
